availableCommands.name: audit-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Try to fool a repo's verification skill, either kind made by /create-prove-it (the permanent prove-<app> or a temporary prove-<migration>). Plants one deliberate bug at a time in the files the current change touched (or along a flow the user names), and for a migration only in the new system, never the old one it is compared with. A fresh agent then checks that change or flow with the skill and its answer keys, without knowing what was planted. Records whether it caught the bug, reverts exactly, and reports every miss with a suggested fix to the skill and to the flow's answer key. Use for /audit-prove-it, "can the verifier be fooled", "test the verify skill", "is our verification any good", "mutation test the verifier", or after creating or heavily editing a prove-* skill.

availableCommands.name: create-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that an agent runs at the end of a change, before it says done. It asks first whether the skill is for the app or for a migration. For the app it writes or extends one permanent prove-<app> skill with a section per surface (web, API, MCP, CLI), and a new surface adds a section, not a new skill. For a migration (Python to Rust, Next.js to React Router) it writes a temporary prove-<migration> skill that runs old and new side by side, then hands its cases to prove-<app> as snapshots when the old system is deleted. It checks what the change touches (the new flows it adds and the existing flows it touched), each against an answer key the builder did not write, such as an old system, a snapshot, a test suite or the user's spec. Use for /create-prove-it, "set up verification", "make a verify skill for this repo", "I'm adding an MCP server" or any new surface, "verify this migration", or "the agent keeps saying done without testing".

availableCommands.name: maintain-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Improve a repo's generated verification skill from what its past runs learned. Works on both kinds made by /create-prove-it, the permanent prove-<app> and a temporary prove-<migration>. Reads the receipts in .prove-it/runs/ (failed and blocked steps, retries, the commands that finally worked, steps that failed for reasons unrelated to the change, how each change was sorted into checks) and any bug that slipped past prove, then fixes drifted steps, writes in the working commands, adds the check that would have caught a slipped bug and a section for any new surface. For a temporary skill it checks whether the migration is done and, if so, suggests the end step. Never rewrites an answer key (spec, snapshot, old system) to match the app. Proves every edit live and reports product bugs without touching product code. Use for /maintain-prove-it, "update the verify skill", "the verifier is out of date", "prove missed this bug", "prove keeps failing on unrelated steps", or after a big merge or migration milestone.

It asks first whether the skill is for the app or for a migration. For the app it writes or extends one permanent prove-<app> skill with a section per surface (web, API, MCP, CLI), and a new surface adds a section, not a new skill. For a migration (Python to Rust, Next.js to React Router) it writes a temporary prove-<migration> skill that runs old and new side by side, then hands its cases to prove-<app> as snapshots when the old system is deleted. It checks what the change touches (the new flows it adds and the existing flows it touched), each against an answer key the builder did not write, such as an old system, a snapshot, a test suite or the user's spec. Use for /create-prove-it, "set up verification", "make a verify skill for this repo", "I'm adding an MCP server" or any new surface, "verify this migration", or "the agent keeps saying done without testing".

availableCommands.name: maintain-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Improve a repo's generated verification skill from what its past runs learned. Works on both kinds made by /create-prove-it, the permanent prove-<app> and a temporary prove-<migration>. Reads the receipts in .prove-it/runs/ (failed and blocked steps, retries, the commands that finally worked, steps that failed for reasons unrelated to the change, how each change was sorted into checks) and any bug that slipped past prove, then fixes drifted steps, writes in the working commands, adds the check that would have caught a slipped bug and a section for any new surface. For a temporary skill it checks whether the migration is done and, if so, suggests the end step. Never rewrites an answer key (spec, snapshot, old system) to match the app. Proves every edit live and reports product bugs without touching product code. Use for /maintain-prove-it, "update the verify skill", "the verifier is out of date", "prove missed this bug", "prove keeps failing on unrelated steps", or after a big merge or migration milestone.

availableCommands.name: audit-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Try to fool a repo's verification skill, either kind made by /create-prove-it (the permanent prove-<app> or a temporary prove-<migration>). Plants one deliberate bug at a time in the files the current change touched (or along a flow the user names), and for a migration only in the new system, never the old one it is compared with. A fresh agent then checks that change or flow with the skill and its answer keys, without knowing what was planted. Records whether it caught the bug, reverts exactly, and reports every miss with a suggested fix to the skill and to the flow's answer key. Use for /audit-prove-it, "can the verifier be fooled", "test the verify skill", "is our verification any good", "mutation test the verifier", or after creating or heavily editing a prove-* skill.

availableCommands.name: create-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that an agent runs at the end of a change, before it says done. It asks first whether the skill is for the app or for a migration. For the app it writes or extends one permanent prove-<app> skill with a section per surface (web, API, MCP, CLI), and a new surface adds a section, not a new skill. For a migration (Python to Rust, Next.js to React Router) it writes a temporary prove-<migration> skill that runs old and new side by side, then hands its cases to prove-<app> as snapshots when the old system is deleted. It checks what the change touches (the new flows it adds and the existing flows it touched), each against an answer key the builder did not write, such as an old system, a snapshot, a test suite or the user's spec. Use for /create-prove-it, "set up verification", "make a verify skill for this repo", "I'm adding an MCP server" or any new surface, "verify this migration", or "the agent keeps saying done without testing".

availableCommands.name: maintain-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Improve a repo's generated verification skill from what its past runs learned. Works on both kinds made by /create-prove-it, the permanent prove-<app> and a temporary prove-<migration>. Reads the receipts in .prove-it/runs/ (failed and blocked steps, retries, the commands that finally worked, steps that failed for reasons unrelated to the change, how each change was sorted into checks) and any bug that slipped past prove, then fixes drifted steps, writes in the working commands, adds the check that would have caught a slipped bug and a section for any new surface. For a temporary skill it checks whether the migration is done and, if so, suggests the end step. Never rewrites an answer key (spec, snapshot, old system) to match the app. Proves every edit live and reports product bugs without touching product code. Use for /maintain-prove-it, "update the verify skill", "the verifier is out of date", "prove missed this bug", "prove keeps failing on unrelated steps", or after a big merge or migration milestone.

availableCommands.name: audit-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Try to fool a repo's verification skill, either kind made by /create-prove-it (the permanent prove-<app> or a temporary prove-<migration>). Plants one deliberate bug at a time in the files the current change touched (or along a flow the user names), and for a migration only in the new system, never the old one it is compared with. A fresh agent then checks that change or flow with the skill and its answer keys, without knowing what was planted. Records whether it caught the bug, reverts exactly, and reports every miss with a suggested fix to the skill and to the flow's answer key. Use for /audit-prove-it, "can the verifier be fooled", "test the verify skill", "is our verification any good", "mutation test the verifier", or after creating or heavily editing a prove-* skill.

availableCommands.name: create-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that an agent runs at the end of a change, before it says done. It asks first whether the skill is for the app or for a migration. For the app it writes or extends one permanent prove-<app> skill with a section per surface (web, API, MCP, CLI), and a new surface adds a section, not a new skill. For a migration (Python to Rust, Next.js to React Router) it writes a temporary prove-<migration> skill that runs old and new side by side, then hands its cases to prove-<app> as snapshots when the old system is deleted. It checks what the change touches (the new flows it adds and the existing flows it touched), each against an answer key the builder did not write, such as an old system, a snapshot, a test suite or the user's spec. Use for /create-prove-it, "set up verification", "make a verify skill for this repo", "I'm adding an MCP server" or any new surface, "verify this migration", or "the agent keeps saying done without testing".

availableCommands.name: maintain-prove-it
availableCommands.description: Improve a repo's generated verification skill from what its past runs learned. Works on both kinds made by /create-prove-it, the permanent prove-<app> and a temporary prove-<migration>. Reads the receipts in .prove-it/runs/ (failed and blocked steps, retries, the commands that finally worked, steps that failed for reasons unrelated to the change, how each change was sorted into checks) and any bug that slipped past prove, then fixes drifted steps, writes in the working commands, adds the check that would have caught a slipped bug and a section for any new surface. For a temporary skill it checks whether the migration is done and, if so, suggests the end step. Never rewrites an answer key (spec, snapshot, old system) to match the app. Proves every edit live and reports product bugs without touching product code. Use for /maintain-prove-it, "update the verify skill", "the verifier is out of date", "prove missed this bug", "prove keeps failing on unrelated steps", or after a big merge or migration milestone.

availableCommands.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

availableCommands.name: diagnose-crash
availableCommands.description: Diagnose why a program crashed on this machine, from a systemd-coredump core dump. Use when a process has segfaulted, aborted, or otherwise dumped core, when asked why an application crashed or disappeared, or when a "Process crashed:" desktop notification is acted on. Triggers: crash, segfault, SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, core dump, coredumpctl, "why did X crash", "X keeps crashing", backtrace symbolization. Covers reporting a confirmed Omarchy bug upstream — see reporting.md.

availableCommands.name: diagnosing-bugs
availableCommands.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

availableCommands.name: domain-modeling
availableCommands.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

availableCommands.name: find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

availableCommands.name: get-subtitles
availableCommands.description: Extract subtitles or transcripts from YouTube videos and local video files. Use when the user wants subtitles, captions, or transcripts from a video, or asks to "get the transcript of this video."

availableCommands.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
availableCommands.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.

availableCommands.name: grill-me
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

availableCommands.name: grill-with-docs
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

availableCommands.name: grilling
availableCommands.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

availableCommands.name: handoff
availableCommands.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

availableCommands.name: implement
availableCommands.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

availableCommands.name: implement-spec
availableCommands.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture
availableCommands.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

availableCommands.name: loop-me
availableCommands.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
availableCommands.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

availableCommands.name: omarchy
availableCommands.description: REQUIRED for end-user customization of Linux desktop, window manager, or system config. Use when editing ANY file in ~/.config/, ~/.config/hypr/, ~/.config/omarchy/, ~/.config/alacritty/, ~/.config/foot/, ~/.config/kitty/, or ~/.config/ghostty/. Triggers: Hyprland, window rules, window behavior, animations, keybindings, monitors, gaps, borders, blur, opacity, omarchy-shell, bar, widgets, terminal config, themes, fonts, background, night light, idle, lock screen, screenshots, screen recording, reminders, layer rules, workspace settings, display config, appearance changes, and user-facing omarchy commands. Excludes Omarchy source development through `omarchy dev link` workflows.

availableCommands.name: omarchy-app
availableCommands.description: Build a new desktop app for Omarchy the way Omarchy's own apps are built (Hype, Monologue, Omacut): C++ and Qt Quick, compiled with qmake6 and make into a single binary, following the Omarchy theme live, and installed as an Arch package so it shows up in the app launcher. Use when asked to make, build, or scaffold an app, tool, utility, or GUI program for the desktop. Triggers: new app, make me an app, desktop app, GUI, Qt, QML, Qt Quick, C++ app, qmake, app launcher entry, PKGBUILD for my app.

availableCommands.name: openspec-apply-change
availableCommands.description: Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change. Use when the user wants to start implementing, continue implementation, or work through tasks. Also use when the user says "openspec apply", "opsx apply", or "openspec implement".

availableCommands.name: openspec-archive-change
availableCommands.description: Archive a completed OpenSpec change in the experimental workflow. Use when the user wants to finalize and archive a change after implementation is complete. Also use when the user says "openspec archive" or "opsx archive".

availableCommands.name: openspec-explore
availableCommands.description: Enter OpenSpec explore mode - a thinking partner for exploring ideas, investigating problems, and clarifying requirements in a project that uses OpenSpec. Use when the user wants to think through something before or during an OpenSpec change. Also use when the user says "openspec explore" or "opsx explore".

availableCommands.name: openspec-propose
availableCommands.description: Propose a new OpenSpec change with all artifacts generated in one step. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation. Also use when the user says "openspec propose" or "opsx propose".

availableCommands.name: openspec-sync-specs
availableCommands.description: Sync delta specs from an OpenSpec change to main specs. Use when the user wants to update main specs with changes from a delta spec, without archiving the change. Also use when the user says "openspec sync" or "opsx sync".

availableCommands.name: openspec-update-change
availableCommands.description: Update an OpenSpec change by revising its existing planning artifacts and keeping them coherent with one another. Use when the user wants to revise a change's plan, fold new decisions into it, or reconcile its artifacts after an edit. Also use when the user says "openspec update change" or "opsx update". If the user means the openspec update CLI command, which refreshes generated files, run that command instead. Never edits code.

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Use when writing a PR body.

availableCommands.name: prototype
availableCommands.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

availableCommands.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
availableCommands.description: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.

availableCommands.name: retro
availableCommands.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

availableCommands.name: scaffold-exercises
availableCommands.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.

availableCommands.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
availableCommands.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

availableCommands.name: setup-pre-commit
availableCommands.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

availableCommands.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
availableCommands.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.

availableCommands.name: superwhisper
availableCommands.description: Configure and troubleshoot Superwhisper dictation on Linux through its CLI. Use when the user asks to change or inspect Superwhisper: processing mode (Offline, Offline Lite, Cloud), language, tone, microphone, keyboard shortcuts, sound effects, the recording indicator, silence removal, auto-paste, history and retention, vocabulary and replacements, offline model downloads, launch at login, the Omarchy bar panel, or why dictation is not working. Triggers: superwhisper, dictation, speech to text, push to talk, voice typing.

availableCommands.name: tdd
availableCommands.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

availableCommands.name: teach
availableCommands.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

availableCommands.name: to-issues
availableCommands.description: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices. Use when user wants to convert a plan into issues, create implementation tickets, or break down work into issues.

availableCommands.name: to-prd
availableCommands.description: Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker. Use when user wants to create a PRD from the current context.

availableCommands.name: to-questionnaire
availableCommands.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

availableCommands.name: to-spec
availableCommands.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

availableCommands.name: to-tickets
availableCommands.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

availableCommands.name: wait-what
availableCommands.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

availableCommands.name: wizard
availableCommands.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

availableCommands.name: write-a-skill
availableCommands.description: Create new agent skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and bundled resources. Use when user wants to create, write, or build a new skill.

availableCommands.name: writing-beats
availableCommands.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.

availableCommands.name: writing-for-agents
availableCommands.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

availableCommands.name: writing-fragments
availableCommands.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.

availableCommands.name: writing-shape
availableCommands.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.

availableCommands.name: zoom-out
availableCommands.description: Tell the agent to zoom out and give broader context or a higher-level perspective. Use when you're unfamiliar with a section of code or need to understand how it fits into the bigger picture.

availableCommands.name: factory:factory-intent
availableCommands.description: Écrire ou rafraîchir l'intention d'une tâche avant de toucher au code — objectif, non-objectifs, critères d'acceptation. À utiliser au début de toute tâche non triviale, ou quand FACTORY L1 refuse une écriture faute d'intention.

availableCommands.name: factory:factory-learn
availableCommands.description: Distiller ce qu'une session vient d'apprendre — une leçon vérifiée dans `.factory/lessons.md` et, si le savoir est réutilisable, une skill ou une mise à jour de skill. À utiliser en fin de tâche non triviale, après une erreur coûteuse, ou quand l'utilisateur a corrigé une approche.

availableCommands.name: factory:factory-remember
availableCommands.description: Mémoriser un fait durable (convention, commande, décision d'architecture, préférence) dans la mémoire du projet ou les préférences utilisateur. À utiliser quand l'utilisateur corrige, précise une convention, ou quand un fait sera encore vrai dans une semaine.

availableCommands.name: factory:factory-status
availableCommands.description: Afficher ou faire monter le palier de maturité de la factory (L0 observe → L4 evidence) et vérifier les conditions mécaniques de promotion. À utiliser quand l'utilisateur demande où en est la factory, ou pourquoi un hook bloque.

availableCommands.name: factory:factory-verify
availableCommands.description: Vérifier indépendamment un changement avant de conclure — tests, lint, typecheck, build — et produire la preuve. À utiliser après toute modification de code, ou quand FACTORY L3 a bloqué une clôture faute de vérification.

availableCommands.name: gitnexus:gitnexus-debugging
availableCommands.description: Debug a bug, trace an error, find why something fails using GitNexus knowledge graph

availableCommands.name: gitnexus:gitnexus-exploring
availableCommands.description: Understand architecture, trace execution flows, explore unfamiliar code using GitNexus knowledge graph

availableCommands.name: gitnexus:gitnexus-impact-analysis
availableCommands.description: Know what breaks before changing something using GitNexus blast radius analysis

availableCommands.name: gitnexus:gitnexus-pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR, assess merge risk, check blast radius using GitNexus knowledge graph

availableCommands.name: gitnexus:gitnexus-refactoring
availableCommands.description: Rename, extract, split, or restructure code safely using GitNexus knowledge graph
